Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):  Right knee pain with clicking during exercise, onset ~2 weeks ago; pain begins ~20 minutes into runs, led to stopping last run; no pain at rest; initial mild swelling after first run resolved with ice; no persistent swelling, redness, heat, locking, or instability; full ROM. One episode of tingling in right toes after a run; occasional sock indentation after prolonged standing (dependent edema).  
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):  Not recorded  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:  Ibuprofen 400 mg PRN for pain; route/frequency not fully documented. Aleve (naproxen) — dose/route/frequency not documented. Vitamin D — dose/route/frequency not documented. Melatonin — dose/route/frequency not documented. Alprazolam (Xanax) occasionally for sleep — dose/route/frequency not documented. Cannabis (smoked joint) occasionally.  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus):  Not recorded  
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks:  Not recorded  
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use:  Highly active; training for a marathon (runs up to ~7–8 miles), gym several times/week, plays sports including ice hockey. Tobacco: not recorded. Alcohol: not recorded. Substance use: occasional cannabis. Diet: not recorded.  
- Hearing and vision concerns:  Vision: farsighted; prior LASIK surgery. Hearing: Not recorded

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Summary: Adult runner with 2-week history of right knee pain and clicking provoked by running after ~20 minutes and by repetitive flexion/extension during gym exercises; initial transient swelling resolved with ice; no mechanical locking, giving way, or stair/walking limitation; full ROM. Single episode of right toe tingling post-run; no persistent neurovascular symptoms.  
- Working diagnosis: Overuse running-related knee pain most consistent with iliotibial band friction syndrome versus patellofemoral pain syndrome.  
- Reasoning: Onset after increase in running load, lateral/central knee discomfort, activity-provoked pain and clicking without instability or locking, improvement with rest/ice support ITB friction or PFPS.  
- Considerations (from DDx, consistent with transcript):  
  - Meniscal irritation/degenerative tear (low–medium likelihood): clicking and one episode of post-activity swelling, though no locking, joint line tenderness, or clear twisting injury.  
  - Transient peripheral nerve irritation/footwear-related cause for toe tingling (low likelihood).  
- Management:  
  - Continue ice therapy.  
  - Reduce running load; avoid running through pain.  
  - NSAIDs: continue ibuprofen PRN; a stronger anti-inflammatory was prescribed to pharmacy (specific agent/dose not recorded). Do not take concurrently with ibuprofen; take with food.  
  - Referral to physiotherapy for comprehensive knee assessment and guided rehab.  
  - Imaging to be considered after physiotherapy assessment if symptoms persist or exam suggests intra-articular pathology (e.g., cartilage/meniscal).  
  - Safety-net: seek urgent care if persistent swelling, warmth/redness, fever, systemic illness, or if knee locks and cannot bend/straighten.  
- Conflicts: None noted between transcript and DDx. (Medication identity clarification: patient unsure if Aleve is acetaminophen; Aleve is naproxen.)

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:  Education provided on rest/ice, avoiding painful activity, safe NSAID use with food, and red-flag symptoms requiring urgent review.  
- Patient health goals and priorities:  Continue marathon training; resolve knee pain to return to running.  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA):  Not recorded  
- Referrals (allied health, Quitline, AOD services, Aboriginal health worker, or social supports):  Physiotherapy referral placed.  
- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled:  Not recorded; advised to return if red flags or if physiotherapy wait is prolonged; clinic visit available.

Consider

- Mental health support or counselling referral:  Not recorded  
- Specialist referral for complex chronic disease management:  Not recorded  
- Dental referral if oral health issues identified:  Not recorded  
- Optometry referral for visual concerns or regular screening:  Not recorded  
- Audiometry referral if hearing issues suspected:  Not recorded  
- Social work or housing support referral if social determinants affect health:  Not recorded  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Iliotibial band friction syndrome (High): Lateral-predominant exercise-induced knee pain starting after several miles with increased running load and clicking during flexion/extension, without locking or instability.  
- Patellofemoral pain syndrome (Medium): Overuse anterior/retropatellar pain pattern with crepitus provoked by running and repeated knee motion after training load increase; location not clearly anterior.  
- Meniscal pathology (Low–Medium): Clicking and one episode of swelling could fit, but lack of locking, joint line tenderness, or twisting injury lowers likelihood.

- Internal conflicts or contradictions: None significant.  
- Transcript quality notes: Video/telehealth consultation; no in-person physical exam performed; history otherwise clear and consistent.
